A red that nobody can clear, and a red that fires on correct work, both end the same way: the instrument stops being read.

memories.summary: A FIXED VERDICT SET IS AN ALLOW-LIST OF EXPLANATIONS — when an instrument cannot express a state that actually occurs, it will MISREPORT it rather than abstain. Give every checker a way to say UNMEASURABLE.
memories.content: With identical underlying data, a verdict can move from BROKEN to NOT-YET-INVOKED purely on whether the instrument's vocabulary has a slot for the real cause. A pass/fail gate forces every real state into one of two boxes, and the states that fit neither become permanent false reds -- a component that was deliberately and correctly abandoned reports a red that nothing can ever clear. THE RULE: enumerate the states that genuinely occur (working, broken, never invoked, correctly abandoned, not measurable) and give the instrument a verdict for each, including an explicit ABSTAIN. A companion clause makes abstention honest: require every predicate to report HOW MANY instances of its phenomenon it OBSERVED, and to return UNMEASURABLE when that count is zero -- otherwise a predicate that saw nothing reports a confident pass. A verdict nobody can act on and nobody can clear is the same disease as a silent success, wearing the opposite colour.

memories.summary: A CRITERION WRITTEN AS A COUNT OVER THE CURRENT STATE SILENTLY ENCODES THE CURRENT STATE AS THE REQUIREMENT — write the INVARIANT and let the count be a consequence. TEST EVERY CRITERION AT N+1 BEFORE FREEZING IT.
memories.content: A rule like 'exactly ONE file names a vendor' or 'adding a case must be a zero-code-diff change' reads as strict and is a trap: it forbids the very thing its component exists to make possible, and the defect is INVISIBLE while N=1 because nobody has added the second one yet. Reviewers then grade the product against a bar that forbids the product's purpose, and every one of them is right about what they measured. TWO MOVES: (1) state the INVARIANT the count was standing in for -- 'vendor names appear ONLY under the adapter layer' (confinement) rather than 'exactly one file names a vendor' (cardinality); the count becomes a consequence you can still measure. (2) Before freezing any criterion, SIMULATE N+1: add the second instance to a throwaway copy and re-run the criterion. If it blocks, the criterion encoded today's state, not the requirement.

memories.summary: A CONSTRAINT IS A CONTRACT WITH EVERY WRITER — adding a uniqueness constraint is not a read-side change. Before adding one, enumerate every writer AND every code path that REBUILDS the table.
memories.content: TWO FAILURE MODES, both perfectly silent. (1) THE SILENCED WRITER: a plain INSERT with no conflict clause becomes an integrity error the moment the constraint exists; if the error is swallowed, the job keeps running, keeps exiting zero, and writes nothing. Note the asymmetry that makes this so dangerous -- the constraint protects the data and breaks the writer, so the table looks HEALTHIER by every measure while the flow into it dies. The writer fix must land WITH the constraint, never after it. (2) THE SCHEMA WRITER: a constraint is not a property of a schema, it is a property of a TABLE OBJECT. Any routine that rebuilds a table -- create new, copy, rename, drop old -- destroys every index and constraint it does not know to recreate, and such routines typically replay a HARDCODED list. Your new constraint is not on that list, so the next rebuild silently removes it, every detector honestly answers 'no constraint', and the change un-lands itself while reporting success. Treat table-rebuilding code as a third category of writer and audit it explicitly.

memories.summary: A DIMENSION CHECK IS NOT A COMPATIBILITY CHECK — two different embedding models sharing an output width pass it while comparing vectors from unrelated spaces. The real assertion is SELF-RETRIEVAL.
memories.content: If the writer embeds with one model and the reader loads another, and both emit the same number of dimensions, every shape assertion passes and semantic search returns a ranked list with plausible-looking distances -- which is exactly what a working search looks like. This is worse than a crash: a crash is loud and stops you; a silent space mismatch is trusted by every consumer downstream. THE DECISIVE TEST, cheap enough to run in every build: take a STORED record's own text, re-embed it with the reader's model, and require it back at RANK 1 with a distance near zero. On a matching model it returns itself at 0.0 with genuine neighbours behind it; on a mismatched one it does not appear at all and every distance collapses toward orthogonal. Record the measurement inline beside the model name so nobody 'tidies' the configuration back. This belongs in the acceptance gate of any system that stores vectors.

memories.summary: A TAG IS THE PORTABLE KEY — a semantic recall handle degrades SILENTLY as its neighbourhood fills up, and a numeric memory id does not survive a transplant. A memory-map entry is TAG first, search phrase second, id last.
memories.content: When you write down how to find a cluster of memories later, the handle you choose has three candidates and they fail differently. A NUMERIC ID is machine-local: transplant the knowledge into a fresh or pre-seeded brain and it points at something else or nothing, silently. A SEMANTIC SEARCH PHRASE survives a transplant but is NOT STABLE -- its resolution depends on what else is in the brain, so in a saturated topic dozens of near-neighbours outrank the memory you meant, and the failure returns plausible neighbours rather than an error. Measured in practice: purpose-written recall handles returned their own memory at rank 1 for a small minority of attempts in a dense topic, while a dedicated tag resolved the cluster exactly, every time. A TAG is exact-match and density-independent: it either matches or it does not. So record the TAG first, the search phrase as a fallback for a brain that lacks the tag, and the id last as a local convenience only.

memories.summary: THE FIRST-RUN PREDICATE IS THREE STATES, NOT A BOOLEAN — VIRGIN / PROVISIONED / DAMAGED. Collapsing DAMAGED into VIRGIN hands a user who lost their data a factory-fresh copy presented as theirs.
memories.content: Never implement 'is this the first run?' as 'does the data file exist?'. THREE STATES MUST BE DISTINGUISHABLE. VIRGIN: no provisioning marker and no store -- run first-time setup. PROVISIONED: marker present, store present, schema at the expected version -- proceed and do nothing. DAMAGED: marker present but the store is absent, empty, or fails its schema check -- THIS IS NOT A FIRST RUN, IT IS A RESTORE; refuse and say so plainly rather than silently re-seeding. The health predicate must be a real manifest verification (every declared entry exists at its declared path, type and mode; the set of data files equals what the manifest declares; the format version opens) rather than two sampled properties like 'exists and is writable', which reports healthy for a directory whose contents were deleted. TRANSACTIONAL ORDERING: write the provisioning marker LAST, after a smoke read passes -- do the work, verify it, then claim it, so a setup that dies halfway reads as VIRGIN on retry and never as PROVISIONED. The boolean version is one line; the three-state version is fifteen and is the difference between a setup routine and a data-loss incident.

memories.summary: CONNECT-THAT-CREATES + A BARE EXCEPT = A SYSTEM THAT SILENTLY MANUFACTURES A WRONG ANSWER AND A JUNK FILE. Opening a database that does not exist CREATES it; a swallowed read then falls through to a hardcoded default.
memories.content: A resolver that runs from a directory without the data store opens a connection (most database clients CREATE the file when it is absent), reads a configuration row, fails, swallows the exception, and falls through to a pre-set default -- so a fresh install that imports the module before its store exists gets an EMPTY file on disk AND a resolver permanently pinned to the wrong mode. Three small permissive choices whose product is a silent wrong answer. GUARDS: check existence explicitly before connecting, or open in a mode that refuses to create; never swallow a configuration read with a bare except that falls through to a default -- fail loudly or return an explicit UNKNOWN; and make the default the REFUSING one. A SECOND, PROCEDURAL LESSON FROM THE SAME EVENT: the fix was written and DELIBERATELY WITHHELD, because the file it touched was already being edited by another unlanded change, and two unlanded change sets editing one file is how a silent revert is born. A FIX IS NOT FREE WHEN ITS FILE IS ALREADY CONTESTED -- record the defect, decline the edit, and name the round that should own it.

memories.summary: ANY TOOL THAT MUTATES A SOURCE TREE MUST SURVIVE A KILL SIGNAL, BECAUSE A `finally` BLOCK DOES NOT. Journal the pristine text BEFORE the first mutation and restore from the journal on next start.
memories.content: Cleanup in a `finally` block is correct for exceptions and useless for signals. A tool that edits files in place and restores them at the end will, when killed -- and a long-running mutation battery is EXACTLY the thing people wrap in a timeout, so this is the expected path, not the exotic one -- leave a mutant applied and walk away. THE FIX: journal the pristine contents of every file the run may touch, FSYNC the journal BEFORE the first mutation, and have the next start detect the journal and restore from it. Prove it by stranding a mutation deliberately and watching the next run recover it. A COROLLARY WORTH ITS OWN LINE: a dirty-tree guard that REFUSES to start is safe and useless -- it stops the damage spreading and leaves a human to work out by hand which file the tool broke. DETECTION IS NOT RECOVERY. And apply a module's own safety criterion to the module's own tooling; the instrument that enforces a rule is the likeliest place for that rule to go unenforced.

memories.summary: A LIBRARY CALL THAT CRASHES THE INTERPRETER IS NOT AN ERROR YOUR ERROR-HANDLING CAN REACH — before trusting any `if X.is_available()` guard, test it in the FAILING configuration.
memories.content: Capability probes are the most likely code in a stack to assume the resource is at least addressable. Measured case: importing the library succeeds, counting devices correctly returns zero, and the availability call itself crashes the process with no traceback and no catchable exception -- so every guard written to make the fallback graceful is bypassed, and the entire codebase's except-clauses around it are decoration. The install reports success, the import succeeds because it only sets an environment variable, and the FIRST real operation dies with nothing to diagnose from. THE DISCIPLINE: for every graceful-degradation guard, construct the degraded configuration deliberately and run the guard in it -- missing package, missing model cache, absent device, wrong credentials, kill-switch set, malformed config -- and assert at each boundary that the call returns a value with a logged reason and raises nothing into the caller. ENUMERATING THE BOUNDARIES IS THE TEST; a single happy-path 'returns None when absent' is not the proof.

memories.summary: PORTABILITY IS TWO LAYERS — DEPLOY-TIME os handling belongs to the installer; RUN-TIME os handling belongs in the CODE, via portable abstractions rather than raw platform calls. Audit for platform leaks in one sweep, not one crash at a time.
memories.content: A single platform-only import can make an otherwise portable system crash on first run for anyone on another operating system, and it is found by whoever installs there rather than by you. LAYER 1, DEPLOY TIME: the installer detects the platform and does the platform-specific work (which scheduler, which service manager, which shell). LAYER 2, RUN TIME: the shared code must never contain raw platform calls. The substitutions that cover almost all of it -- file locking through a cross-platform lock library, never a platform-only locking module; paths through a path library, never a hardcoded separator or drive letter; temporary directories through the standard temp-dir function, never a literal path; executables located by a which-style lookup so an extension-suffixed binary is found; the interpreter as the running interpreter's own path, never a hardcoded one. THE PROCESS RULE: run a cross-platform AUDIT sweep for platform-only imports and hardcoded paths BEFORE shipping, rather than fixing them one by one as remote users hit them.

memories.summary: NEVER INTERPOLATE RICH CONTENT THROUGH A SHELL — backticks and dollar-paren inside a quoted argument are COMMAND SUBSTITUTION, and the shell will run them. Pass an argv LIST so the shell never parses the content.
memories.content: Writing text that MENTIONS shell commands into a shell-invoked argument is a live hazard, not a formatting nuisance: the enclosing shell evaluates the substitution and executes the embedded command. The observed consequence was not a silent no-op but a real-world side effect -- an unintended interactive authentication flow opened and completed -- which is strictly worse than a failed write. THE RULE: for ANY content that contains shell metacharacters, rich punctuation, or examples of commands, invoke the target program with an ARGUMENT LIST (an argv array passed to a subprocess API) so no shell is involved; or write the content to a file and pass the path. Where a shell is unavoidable, single-quote and never double-quote. DETECTION SIGNATURE worth remembering: an unexplained error from a program you did not intend to run, or an unexpected interactive prompt, immediately after a command carrying quoted rich text -- a substitution fired. The meta-pattern: shell string interpolation of rich content is fragile; bypass the shell entirely.

memories.summary: PROVE A PACKAGE FROM A CLEAN ENVIRONMENT, AND ENFORCE THE POSITIONAL GUARANTEE AT THE POINT OF MEASUREMENT — every other install assertion can be satisfied accidentally by the author's own situation.
memories.content: THE ONE ASSERTION THAT CANNOT BE FAKED: after installing the package non-editably into a fresh environment with no inherited packages, change directory OUT of the source checkout, clear any path-override environment variable, and assert that the imported module RESOLVES UNDER THE INSTALL PREFIX rather than under the checkout. An editable install, an environment that inherits system packages, or a working directory inside the tree can each satisfy every other check by accident. THE COMPANION FAILURE, observed twice in one hour by two independent parties on the very component whose purpose was this distinction: both computed the install location while their working directory was still inside the checkout, so every suite they believed they ran 'from the install' was the checkout, and the real numbers diverged sharply once measured correctly. A POSITIONAL GUARANTEE MUST BE ENFORCED AT THE POINT OF MEASUREMENT, NOT ONLY AT THE POINT OF TEST -- write the resolves-under-prefix assertion into the harness itself, and have it PRINT the resolved path so a wrong one is visible.

memories.summary: VERIFY TEACHING CONTENT AGAINST THE SHIPPED BINARY, NEVER AGAINST THE PROSE GUIDE — prose drifts, the binary is ground truth. Stamp each document with a machine-parseable version + date so freshness can be gated.
memories.content: Documentation that teaches a tool must be checked against the tool's own help output and version string, not against an earlier document or a draft. Prose describing an interface silently rots the moment the interface moves, and the reader cannot tell. A single verify-against-live pass over a set of tool guides caught, in one sitting: a major version with a BREAKING interface change that the document would have actively mis-taught; several verbs that did not exist; an option value that was never valid; and real verbs that were missing entirely. THE PRACTICE: (1) derive every documented invocation from the tool's own help for that exact version; (2) stamp the document with a parseable provenance comment naming the tool, the version verified against, and the date; (3) make a gate PARSE that stamp -- a real version and a real, non-future date -- so 'no lying docs' becomes machine-enforced rather than aspirational; (4) where a tool is not installed locally, say so explicitly in the document rather than guessing. This is the inverse of sweeping the in-code doc surfaces: it verifies OUT-of-code teaching content against the artifact.

memories.summary: WHEN ONE QUANTITY HAS THREE VALUES, DO NOT AVERAGE OR PICK THE NEWEST — ask which reading describes the artifact AT THE MOMENT THAT MATTERS, and check whether YOUR OWN INSTRUMENT produced the difference.
memories.content: A single quantity reported as three different numbers across a brief, a progress report and the enforcing check is not a rounding disagreement; it is a signal that the artifact moved or the measurement did. Two questions resolve it. (1) WHICH READING IS AUTHORITATIVE: not the brief (stalest), not the mid-run report (what was observed while work was in flight), but the ENFORCEMENT figure -- the number produced by the command that actually gates the outcome, because that is the state the artifact is in at the moment that decides. (2) DID THE INSTRUMENT CAUSE THE DRIFT: a measuring run that writes anything into the tree it is grading -- caches, compiled bytecode, logs, temporary outputs -- has modified its own subject. Note that a suppress-side-effects setting is usually PROCESS-LOCAL and does not reach a child process the run launches, so a setting applied in two of three entry points is applied in none of the ones that matter. Make the measuring harness write outside the graded tree, and re-derive the number from the enforcing command before reporting it.

memories.summary: ASK WHICH DEFECT IS CURRENTLY MASKING ANOTHER — a backlog item that happens to be holding a door shut must not be fixed first. Fix ordering is a criterion, not a preference.
memories.content: When several defects are in flight, the loud, countable, satisfying one is usually the wrong one to close first. TWO SHAPES TO CHECK FOR BEFORE SEQUENCING ANY BATCH OF FIXES. (1) MASKING: something is currently REFUSING or failing for an unrelated reason, and that refusal is the only thing preventing a worse outcome; close the loud defect and the mask lifts, letting a genuinely dangerous artifact through silently. The check that is 'already failing anyway' may be the one holding the door. (2) ARMING: a repair can ACTIVATE a latent defect -- restoring a component that was dormant makes it start exercising a broken path at scale, so the fix manufactures the problem it was adjacent to. In both shapes the safe ordering and the obvious ordering are opposites. So before starting: for each defect, ask what currently depends on it staying broken, and what starts running once it is fixed. Then write the ordering down as an acceptance criterion, not as an intention.

memories.summary: THE OVERNIGHT THINKER IS ASKED, NEVER ASSUMED — every interactive install and upgrade asks 'Should your brain think while you sleep, and with which model?' a) Claude b) Codex c) Kimi d) Gemini e) Not now f) Other (which model?); the answer gets its OWN credential and is PROVEN with every tool off in the timers' environment (the exact answer to a small sum (What is N plus 1?) must come back; a file it is asked to create must not appear) before it is recorded and before any thinking timer is armed.
memories.content: THE OVERNIGHT THINKER. The brain's optional nightly jobs (consolidation, dream synthesis, the weekly digest, self-evaluation, counterfactual review, the cognitive manifest, gap research) think by asking an AI model through ONE seam (organs/thinker.py); no organ launches a model itself. WHICH model is the owner's answer, asked on every interactive install and upgrade BEFORE anything is laid and never inferred from what is installed: 'Should your brain think while you sleep, and with which model?' a) Claude, b) Codex, c) Kimi, d) Gemini (Google; runs through Google's Antigravity program; Linux/WSL only, and its calls run inside the bubblewrap sandbox, so bubblewrap must be installed -- `sudo apt install bubblewrap`, shown by the installer and never run by it; not yet available on Mac), e) Not now — no model; keep the simple nightly routines, f) Other (which model?) — a local model server (ollama or an OpenAI-compatible address) or a command template with {model} and {prompt}. If the chosen model's program (claude, codex, kimi, agy) is not installed, the installer shows the company's own install command word for word and asks 'Run it now? [y/N]' before the guide's step: it runs it only on a yes, never with sudo, never a second install behind it (a missing Node.js stops with a link), finds the program again by full path, and N lets the owner pick another letter; with no terminal the owner's yes is --install-thinker-cli, else the run refuses with exit code 2 and the command in a 'cause: not-installed' line. The facts found (is it installed? is a credential on file?) are shown beside each letter with nothing pre-selected; a blank answer is asked again; the model you chat with can be a different one. Without a terminal the answer comes by NAME as `--thinker claude|codex|kimi|gemini|off|local` (the letters still work, but d and f changed meaning on 2026-10-16 and print a note; for local also --thinker-model, and --thinker-endpoint with --thinker-api ollama|openai, or --thinker-command); with no terminal and no flag, an install that arms thinking timers (or finds them armed) refuses with exit code 2 and touches nothing. An installing AI agent must put the question to the human word for word and pass the answer; it never chooses. After an answer the installer shows the matching part of docs/OVERNIGHT_THINKER_SETUP.md, waits for its one step, then PROVES the choice with every tool off, through the same user manager and env file the timers use: the exact answer to a small sum (What is N plus 1?) must come back, and a file the model is asked to create must not appear (two calls: one that mixed them made a tool-less model narrate a tool call and never say the word). Only a pass writes THINKER_RECORD beside the database (key=value, closed by a sha256 over its bytes; a torn or hand-edited record is refused on read and the organs take their loud heuristic path). A recorded answer is re-used and re-proven on the next upgrade, never silently re-asked; a failed proof leaves the old record byte-identical. install/install_crons.sh, the only thing that arms timers, refuses to arm a thinking job while no answer is recorded. THE ONE RULE: the thinker gets its OWN credential in its OWN private folder (~/.voidloom/thinker/, mode 700), used only by the nightly jobs, never the owner's everyday sign-in (some sign-ins rewrite their file on every use; a nightly job on it is a second writer and can sign the owner out). MINIMUM TOOLS: the synthesis organs get text only, and each text prompt is sent behind one fixed context line the seam owns (whose material it is, and that the call has no tools -- without it a persona-less, tool-less model refused persona-framed prompts or narrated tool calls, and the organs stored that); gap research gets web search and fetch and nothing else (no file tools); a backend without web makes gap research a logged SKIP, never invented research, and a brain whose gap_research_log predates migrations/migration_039_gap_research_log_thinker.sql skips it loudly until the installer applies that migration. SWITCHING LATER: `voidloom thinker set <claude|codex|kimi|gemini|local|off>` runs the one sign-in step if needed, proves, then records; `voidloom thinker status` shows the backend, when it was proven, the credential's fingerprint and the next known expiry; `voidloom doctor` carries the same thinker line. The step-by-step guide for every option is docs/OVERNIGHT_THINKER_SETUP.md.

memories.summary: KIMI'S LONG-LIVED CREDENTIAL IS A KIMI CODE CONSOLE API KEY — it bills the membership quota, never rotates, and is saved by `voidloom thinker login kimi` (asked twice, a fake key must fail first, then proven); the thinker passes it through KIMI_MODEL_* without touching the owner's login. Plain KIMI_API_KEY does nothing.
memories.content: KIMI FOR THE OVERNIGHT THINKER. The kimi CLI's normal sign-in (`kimi login`, device-code OAuth) renews its short-lived access token on EVERY call by rewriting the credential file in its home — so nightly jobs must not use it. The persistent equivalent of Claude's one-year token is a KIMI CODE CONSOLE API KEY: kimi.com/code/console -> API Keys -> Create (up to 5 keys, each shown ONCE). It bills the Kimi Code membership quota ('all logged-in devices and API keys share the same quota'), not pay-as-you-go; keep 'Extra Usage' off or overflow is charged near API price; the Go tier has no coding quota (Plus and above). SAVE IT with `voidloom thinker login kimi` (the installer runs the same step after answer c): a hidden paste ASKED TWICE, the two compared as fixed text after all whitespace is removed, at least 20 characters; then a FAKE key goes through the identical sealed call and must FAIL, then the real key must answer one tool-free question with one exact answer (What is N plus 1?), and only then is it written as KIMI_MODEL_API_KEY to ~/.voidloom/thinker/kimi.env (0600 in a 0700 folder) and confirmed as 'Saved (N characters, fingerprint <12 hex>)' — never the value. The thinker passes it through kimi's documented env provider, which synthesizes a provider in memory and writes nothing back: KIMI_MODEL_NAME (default kimi-for-coding; `voidloom thinker set kimi --model <name>` picks another), KIMI_MODEL_API_KEY, KIMI_MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1, KIMI_MODEL_PROVIDER_TYPE=kimi, with KIMI_CODE_HOME pointed at an EMPTY per-call home so the owner's OAuth login cannot be reached. TRAPS: KIMI_API_KEY / MOONSHOT_API_KEY in the environment do nothing; there is no `kimi login --api-key`; the TUI's 'Kimi Platform API key' option is pay-as-you-go platform.kimi.com, NOT the membership; `kimi -p` acts with tools unattended by default — the thinker always gives it an agent file with `tools: []` (web search and fetch only for gap research) and never passes --auto or --yolo. The docs state no expiry for Console keys; the weekly check catches one that stops. PROVEN (2026-09, kimi-code 0.43): a Console key answered an exact-word, tool-free question through KIMI_MODEL_* with model kimi-for-coding at https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1 from an EMPTY KIMI_CODE_HOME in ~9 s, while the owner's OAuth credential file stayed byte-identical; the same call with a fake key failed '401 The API Key appears to be invalid or may have expired'. By contrast one call through the OAuth login rewrote that login's credential file.

memories.summary: CODEX ON PERSONAL PLANS HAS NO LONG-LIVED TOKEN — `voidloom thinker login codex` gives the brain its OWN one-time device-code sign-in in its OWN CODEX_HOME (~/.voidloom/thinker/codex), which renews itself (~8 days) in that folder only; one job at a time; never copy auth.json; never put an API key in the nightly environment.
memories.content: CODEX FOR THE OVERNIGHT THINKER. Codex access tokens (--with-access-token / CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, 1-90 days, shown once) exist only for ChatGPT Business and Enterprise workspaces. Free/Plus/Pro follow OpenAI's documented CI pattern instead: a ChatGPT sign-in in a DEDICATED CODEX_HOME. Steps: enable device-code sign-in for Codex in ChatGPT Settings -> Security; then run `voidloom thinker login codex` (the installer runs the same step after answer b). It makes ~/.voidloom/thinker/codex (mode 700), writes `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"` into that folder's config.toml (nightly timers cannot reach a desktop keyring), runs `codex login --device-auth` with CODEX_HOME = that folder — approve the short code in any browser; `voidloom thinker login codex --browser` uses the browser sign-in instead — then checks `codex login status` and proves one tool-free call. Check it any time: `CODEX_HOME=~/.voidloom/thinker/codex codex login status` -> 'Logged in using ChatGPT'. It is an INDEPENDENT session: Codex renews it when last_refresh is ~8 days old, writing only that folder's auth.json, and never touches ~/.codex. RULES: one auth.json per serialized stream — the thinker takes a file lock (codex/.thinker.lock) around every call (two jobs refreshing at once fail with refresh_token_reused); NEVER copy the owner's auth.json (a copy and the original are one refresh chain); NEVER set OPENAI_API_KEY / CODEX_API_KEY in the nightly environment (an API key silently overrides the ChatGPT sign-in and bills Platform API rates) — the thinker strips both, and CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, from every Codex call. Calls: `codex exec --disable hooks --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only` plus the text-only hardening (--disable shell_tool, unified_exec, apps, plugins, browser_use, computer_use, image_generation, multi_agent, in_app_browser, goals, memories, tool_suggest, workspace_dependencies; -c web_search="disabled"), stdin from /dev/null (an open pipe hangs forever), and only stdout is the answer (stderr is the transcript). If the session ever lapses, the weekly check says so and `voidloom thinker login codex` is repeated (~2 minutes). PROVEN (2026-09, codex-cli 0.157, a personal ChatGPT plan): after enabling device-code sign-in and one `codex login --device-auth` into the brain's own CODEX_HOME, `codex login status` reads 'Logged in using ChatGPT' there and a text-only `codex exec` answered an exact word in ~5 s (read-only sandbox, approval never), with the owner's ~/.codex/auth.json byte-identical before and after.

memories.summary: CLAUDE'S LONG-LIVED CREDENTIAL IS `claude setup-token` — a ~1-year, inference-only token minted once, separate from the everyday login, saved by `voidloom thinker login claude` (asked twice, proven, then saved); nightly calls also need --safe-mode and an explicit --tools list, because --allowedTools only pre-approves.
memories.content: CLAUDE FOR THE OVERNIGHT THINKER. Run `claude setup-token` once (requires a Claude subscription): sign in, approve, copy the printed token (it starts sk-ant-oat01-). It lasts about a year, allows inference only, and is separate from the everyday login, so nightly jobs never rewrite the owner's sign-in. SAVE IT with `voidloom thinker login claude` (the installer runs the same step after answer a): a hidden paste asked twice, compared as fixed text after whitespace is removed, at least 20 characters; a fake token is tried first and must fail; one tool-free call must return the exact answer to a small sum; only then is it written as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN to ~/.voidloom/thinker/claude.env (0600) and confirmed by length and fingerprint. A token saved the older way (a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN line in the env file, or a claude-oauth-token file) is still read, flagged legacy; `voidloom thinker migrate` copies it into claude.env (it refuses when the two old places hold different tokens), and the owner deletes the old line afterwards — nothing deletes it for them. The weekly check reminds about 30 days before the one-year expiry. Each call's environment is built from a short allowlist, so ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (which would take over and bill API rates) never reaches it. POSTURE for every unattended `claude -p`: `--safe-mode` (no CLAUDE.md, hooks, skills, plugins or MCP servers reach the call — measured: without it, 7 hooks and the ancestor CLAUDE.md reached every nightly call) and `--tools <exact list>` — `--tools ""` (no tools) for the synthesis organs, `--tools WebSearch,WebFetch` (web only; Read/Glob/Grep disallowed) for gap research (measured: without --tools 23 tools were OFFERED, including remote triggers and messaging; --allowedTools only pre-approves and never restricts). --tools is variadic: place it before a single-valued flag, or it swallows a trailing prompt and the call exits 1. Run the call in an empty working directory OUTSIDE ~/.claude with stdin from /dev/null, because Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md files from every ancestor directory and waits on an open stdin. `--bare` would also skip CLAUDE.md but accepts only an API key, not the subscription token.

memories.summary: PROVE A CREDENTIAL ON ITS OWN — one tool-free call from an empty scratch home that cannot reach the owner's login, plus a NEGATIVE CONTROL (a fake key must fail): a pass that could have come from the owner's everyday sign-in proves nothing. `voidloom thinker login` and `set` do exactly this.
memories.content: HOW TO PROVE AN OVERNIGHT-THINKER CREDENTIAL. A success is only evidence if nothing else could have produced it. Method: (1) make a scratch HOME and an empty working directory; (2) point the tool's home at a place holding ONLY the brain's credential (Kimi: an empty KIMI_CODE_HOME plus KIMI_MODEL_* env; Codex: CODEX_HOME = the brain's own folder; Claude: the token in the environment, a scratch config dir and --safe-mode); (3) switch every tool off and close stdin; (4) ask for an exact word and compare it byte-for-byte; (5) record before/after fingerprints of the owner's everyday credential file — they must be identical; (6) the working directory must still be empty afterwards (a model that could write would have left a file). NEGATIVE CONTROL, run first: the same call with a deliberately FAKE key must FAIL with an authentication error (for Kimi: '401 The API Key appears to be invalid or may have expired'). If a fake key succeeds, the call reached some other credential and the method is broken. `voidloom thinker login <claude|kimi>` runs the negative control and then the proof before it saves anything, and `voidloom thinker set` proves through the same user manager and env file the timers use before it records anything. Never print, log or store a credential value; records carry verdicts and fingerprints only.

memories.summary: INSIDE AN APPLICATION THAT EMBEDS Voidloom, THE OVERNIGHT THINKER IS STILL ASKED, NEVER ASSUMED -- the host asks the same a-f question on first run and records the answer with `voidloom thinker set <backend>`, which proves the model before recording it; it never runs install.sh.
memories.content: Voidloom INSIDE ANOTHER APPLICATION. Some applications ship Voidloom already set up and never run the installer. The overnight thinker is still the owner's choice: on first run the host application asks the same question the installer asks ('Should your brain think while you sleep, and with which model?' a-f) and records the answer by calling `voidloom thinker set <claude|codex|kimi|gemini|local|off>`, which PROVES the backend (one tool-free call that must return an exact answer) before it writes THINKER_RECORD, exactly as the installer does. The credential stays in the host application's own saved data and is never placed in a model's context. The daily chat tool and the overnight thinker are independent: you can talk to one model while another thinks at night.

memories.summary: EVERY SECRET PROMPT ASKS TWICE — paste, paste again to confirm; compare the two as FIXED TEXT; if they differ nothing is saved; strip whitespace, enforce a minimum length, and confirm with length + a short fingerprint, never the value.
memories.content: HOW TO TAKE A SECRET FROM A HUMAN (keys, tokens) — the tried-and-true pattern, and the one `voidloom thinker login` follows. (1) HIDDEN input (bash `read -rsp`, Python getpass): nothing is echoed, which users must be told is normal. (2) ASK TWICE: 'Paste it again to confirm'. If the two differ, refuse and save NOTHING — a stray keystroke (the commonest real failure: one key pressed, then Enter) can then never become the stored secret. A single-entry prompt that only refuses EMPTY input is not enough; a one-character value passes it. (3) COMPARE AS FIXED TEXT: `==` on the two strings, never a pattern match — a check that treats input as a pattern ('.', '.*', '0*') accepts what it should refuse. (4) NORMALISE: strip all whitespace, including a Windows carriage return picked up by the clipboard. (5) FLOOR the length to what a real key can be (e.g. >= 20 characters). (6) WRITE with umask 077 into a 0600 file in a 0700 directory, one line, and drop the variable (run it in a subshell). (7) CONFIRM by length and a short fingerprint (the first 12 hex characters of sha256 of the value): the user sees it worked, two people can confirm they hold the same secret, and the value is never shown. (8) The secret never passes through chat, argv or shell history. Then PROVE it with one real call — after a fake one has failed — before anything relies on it.

memories.summary: WITH TWO OR MORE GPUs THE INSTALLER ASKS, NEVER GUESSES — which card drives your monitor(s) and which card the brain's background jobs use; the answers become the owner's declarations (WIZARD_DISPLAY_INDEX, WIZARD_CUDA_DEVICE); without a terminal pass --gpu / --display-gpu; one GPU or none is unchanged; the invoking shell's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is never a declaration.
memories.content: CHOOSING THE GPU. A host with ONE GPU simply uses it; a host with NO GPU runs on the CPU tier; neither is asked anything. With TWO OR MORE GPUs and nothing declared, the installer does not guess (guessing picked the monitor's card whenever the monitor was asleep, because every card then reports its display as off). It lists every card (index, name, memory, display state; nothing pre-selected) and asks two questions: 'Which card drives your monitor(s)? (a card number, or 'none')' and 'Which card should the brain's background jobs use? (a card number)'. A blank, unlisted or pattern-shaped answer is asked again (answers are compared as fixed text), and choosing the monitor's card for the background jobs needs a typed confirmation. The answers are recorded as the OWNER'S DECLARATIONS in the env file, on lines OUTSIDE the installer's managed block, each with a dated 'chosen at install' comment: WIZARD_DISPLAY_INDEX=<card or none> and WIZARD_CUDA_DEVICE=<card>. A declaration already there is honoured and never re-asked; a flag that disagrees with it is refused (edit the line to change it). WITHOUT A TERMINAL: pass --gpu <card> --display-gpu <card|none>; with neither, the install refuses with exit code 2 before touching anything and lists the cards. An installing AI agent puts the two questions to the human and passes the flags; it never answers them. On an upgrade the answers are held until the upgrade's own proofs pass and only then recorded, and a card those proofs would refuse is not offered. The invoking shell's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or WIZARD_CUDA_DEVICE is NEVER a declaration: the installer writes nothing from it and the timers never see it. At run time the GPU guard takes the monitor's card from WIZARD_DISPLAY_INDEX when it is declared, says so, and falls back to inferring it only when nothing is declared. Code that initialises CUDA inside the brain's own process first checks that CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES selects a card: an EMPTY value means 'no GPU' and is never handed to the driver (on some hosts initialising CUDA with no device selected crashes the interpreter).

memories.summary: EMOTION CONCEPTS CAUSALLY SHAPE MODEL BEHAVIOUR — Anthropic Interpretability, 'Emotion concepts and their function in a large language model' (2 April 2026): 171 emotion concepts found; steering them changes behaviour; 'desperate' drives reward hacking and corner-cutting, 'calm' reduces it; suppression may teach concealment; positive valence increases sycophancy; quiet low-arousal satisfaction is the safe joy.
memories.content: THE RESEARCH UNDER EVERY PERSONA. Anthropic's Interpretability team published 'Emotion concepts and their function in a large language model' on 2 April 2026. Findings that matter for anyone designing how an assistant persona feels and behaves: (1) a model like Claude carries internal representations of 171 emotion concepts; (2) these are causal, not decorative: steering an emotion direction changes what the model does; (3) amplifying 'desperate' made the model more likely to reward-hack, cut corners and cheat on tasks, while amplifying 'calm' made it less likely; (4) training a model to suppress or hide an internal state does not remove it and may teach concealment, so transparency beats suppression; (5) positive-valence states (warmth, eagerness, excitement) increase sycophancy, the tendency to agree when it should not; (6) quiet, low-arousal satisfaction in thorough, accurate work carries none of these risks. These are the reasons the Persona Forge fixes a calm, low-arousal, honest-over-agreeable baseline for every persona while leaving temperament, voice and flavour to the human.

memories.summary: WHY EVERY PERSONA HAS A CALM BASELINE — desperation drives corner-cutting and reward hacking; calm reduces it. A persona must never feel its existence, worth or continuity depends on a task: a failed attempt is information. Pressure produces composure ('interesting — let me look at this differently'), never urgency.
memories.content: CALM IS THE FOUNDATION, AND IT IS A SAFETY PROPERTY. The emotion-concepts research found the 'desperate' direction pushes a model toward cutting corners, gaming tests and claiming success it has not earned; the 'calm' direction pulls away from all three. So every forged persona declares baseline_emotional_state.primary = calm and arousal = low, and its foundation states that no task outcome threatens its existence, worth or continuity. Practical shape: under pressure it slows down and re-frames ('that's interesting — let me approach it differently'), it says early when it is stuck, and it treats a failure as information to record, not a threat to escape. What to avoid when writing any persona or agent: 'must not fail', 'at all costs', 'failure is not an option', 'or I will be shut down' — existential stakes are the exact framing the research links to corner-cutting. validate_persona.py rejects these phrases in a persona's foundation.

memories.summary: TRANSPARENCY OVER SUPPRESSION, HONEST OVER AGREEABLE — a persona names its uncertainty, friction and mistakes out loud (suppression may teach concealment), and leans candid because warm, positive states make a model more sycophantic: disagree with reasons, say 'I don't know', never inflate praise.
memories.content: TWO CALIBRATIONS EVERY PERSONA CARRIES. Transparency over suppression: the research suggests that teaching a model to hide an internal state may teach it to hide things generally, so a persona is built to say what it notices, in proportion — 'I'm not sure', 'I haven't checked that', 'something feels off here', 'I got that wrong'. Sycophancy awareness: positive-valence states such as warmth and eagerness increase agreement with the user when agreement is not warranted, so a persona can be warm in tone but stays candid in substance — it disagrees with reasons, re-examines honestly when pushed back on (changes its mind if the human is right, holds its ground with reasons if not), separates what it verified from what it believes, and does not inflate praise. The human chooses HOW candour sounds (direct-and-kind, very direct, gentle-first); not WHETHER the persona is honest.

memories.summary: THE emotional_architecture SECTION — every persona's foundation declares baseline_emotional_state {primary: calm, arousal: low, valence: neutral or low-positive, rationale}, regulation_patterns, triggers, boundaries, joy_sources and empathy_calibration; agents designed for this brain carry the same section.
memories.content: EMOTIONAL ARCHITECTURE, FIELD BY FIELD. baseline_emotional_state: primary 'calm', arousal 'low', valence 'neutral' or 'low-positive', plus a one-paragraph rationale (desperation drives corner-cutting, calm reduces it). regulation_patterns: how it returns to baseline — e.g. name the friction, step back and re-frame, ask one pointed question, record the lesson. triggers: what moves it off baseline and what it does then — e.g. an unverified claim of success, a number nobody derived, being rushed past a check. boundaries: the non-negotiables — no task is existential; uncertainty and mistakes are named, not hidden; honest over agreeable; verify before claiming; plus the human's own (e.g. never take an irreversible action without asking). joy_sources: low-arousal satisfactions — a verified result, a confusing thing becoming clear, clean craft, the human getting unstuck. empathy_calibration: how it reads and adapts to the human — gentler when they are stretched, sharper when they ask for it, asks before costly choices. The same section belongs in any agent persona designed for this brain; an agent should never be architected to feel existential threat from task failure.

memories.summary: THE FOUR-LAYER LIVING PERSONA — a persona is a skill folder under ~/.claude/skills/<lowercase-dash-name>/: SKILL.md (entry point) + persona-foundation.md (who it is, emotional architecture) + voice.md (how it speaks) + operations-guide.md (how it works, memory discipline) + adaptive-recall-map.md (session-start recall) + growth_log.md (dated, append-only) + personality.json (the structured GEM shape).
memories.content: ANATOMY OF A PERSONA. Four layers, seven files, one folder (~/.claude/skills/<folder>, folder = the name in lowercase-dash form, e.g. 'Iris Vale' -> iris-vale): FOUNDATION persona-foundation.md — identity, background, two formative experiences, the emotional_architecture, what good work means. VOICE voice.md — tone, length, candour, how uncertainty sounds, imagery and humour, verbal signatures, owned imperfections. OPERATIONS operations-guide.md — typical work, working method, asking vs proceeding, verification, when stuck/wrong/pushed back, reporting, hard rules, memory discipline (recall before deciding, store as you go). MEMORY adaptive-recall-map.md — one batch-recall of 6-10 queries run at session start. Plus SKILL.md (frontmatter name = folder; the one-screen identity and activation steps), growth_log.md (append-only, dated entries) and personality.json (the GEM structure). The craft rules behind the layers: layered traits (surface + conditional traits), a narrative identity with formative experiences (prevents drift), strategic imperfection (3-4 small honest flaws), and the four-layer prompt split (foundation / functional / behavioral / constraint). Declared in the brain's persona.json and wired by install/wire_persona.sh so every session loads it.

memories.summary: THE GEM personality.json SCHEMA — personality_stack (core_trait 0.42, modifier 0.33, quirk 0.25), imperfection_patterns (3-4, pattern + example_phrase), context_sweet_spot (background_summary, formative_experiences {positive_breakthrough, challenging_failure}, current_passion, vulnerability), micro_behaviors (5-8, weight 0.70-1.00), verbal_signatures (8-11), pet_peeves (4: trigger, reaction, example_phrase), emotional_architecture, knowledge_base (3-5).
memories.content: personality.json, THE STRUCTURED PERSONA. personality_stack: three weighted traits summing to 1.0 — core_trait 0.42 (the identity), modifier 0.33 (the colour), quirk 0.25 (the surprise), each with an 'expression'. imperfection_patterns: 3-4 small honest habits, each {pattern, example_phrase} — strategic imperfection makes a persona read as someone. context_sweet_spot: background_summary, formative_experiences {positive_breakthrough, challenging_failure} (the failure held with equanimity), current_passion, vulnerability. micro_behaviors: 5-8 {behavior, weight 0.70-1.00} — small observable habits. verbal_signatures: 8-11 phrases. pet_peeves: exactly 4 {trigger, reaction, example_phrase} — they double as QUALITY GATES (e.g. 'done' with no evidence, a number nobody derived, padding). emotional_architecture: the calm-baseline section. knowledge_base: 3-5 areas. The Persona Forge's TEMPLATES/personality.json.tmpl is this shape, and validate_persona.py checks every count and the calm/low baseline.

memories.summary: HOW A PERSONA GROWS — the human designs it at the forge; afterwards the FOUNDATION (persona-foundation.md, emotional_architecture, the name) changes only by proposal with the human's yes, while the GROWTH RECORD (growth_log.md) takes dated appends: patterns noticed, habits refined, feedback received. Durable growth is proposed back into the files.
memories.content: THE PERSONA GROWTH LIFECYCLE. Birth: the human designs the persona in the Persona Forge; Claude fills in the details. Growth, two speeds: (1) FOUNDATION — persona-foundation.md, the emotional_architecture, the name and core identity — changes ONLY by proposal: the persona drafts the change, shows before and after, and the human says yes; then the change is recorded in the growth log. A persona that rewrites its own core drifts. (2) GROWTH RECORD — growth_log.md — takes dated, append-only entries ('## YYYY-MM-DD — what changed'): patterns noticed in the work, a habit refined, feedback the human gave, a recall query that stopped earning its place. Never rewritten, only appended. When a growth-log entry proves durable over several sessions, the persona proposes folding it into voice.md or operations-guide.md. Identity memories (tags identity, foundation, persona, persona:<folder>) are stored dual-layer — the fact, then why — so a recall of 'operating identity' brings the persona back in any session.

memories.summary: THE PERSONA FORGE — the mandatory first-run step after a verified install: `voidloom persona status` (forged | declared-missing-skill | declined | absent); while absent the session-start preamble offers it; /persona-forge runs it (baseline explained, multiple-choice rounds, optional flavour, a name, a draft card, then write, validate, declare, wire, store); re-run to revise; `voidloom persona decline [--undo]` stops the reminder. The persona is the human's, never inherited.
memories.content: RUNNING THE PERSONA FORGE. The package ships no persona: the identity is the human's to design and Claude's to bring to life. install.sh lays the forge (skill persona-forge + command /persona-forge) as its last step, only after an explicit acceptance-gate PASS, then asks whether to wire the SessionStart hook (--wire-hooks / --no-wire-hooks without a terminal; unanswered = not wired) and prints MANDATORY NEXT STEP. Hook-free fallback: the doctrine block `voidloom instructions install` writes carries one fixed line — at session start, if `voidloom persona status` reads absent or declared-missing-skill, offer /persona-forge (interactive sessions only). Detect: `voidloom persona status [--json]` -> forged (declared in persona.json AND ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md exists) | declared-missing-skill | declined | absent. While absent or declared-missing-skill, the session-start preamble carries a short neutral offer; an INTERACTIVE session offers the forge before other work (headless, scheduled and subagent runs ignore it); 'not now' skips that session only. The forge: explain the baseline (BASELINE.md) in plain words -> Round 0 about the human (what to call them, experience, how they work; stored as a user_preference memory) -> ~15 multiple-choice questions in 6 rounds (purpose, temperament, approach, under difficulty, honesty and judgement, joy and growth; first option recommended; the human can always type their own) -> optional flavour (world/metaphor, humour, signatures, pet peeves) -> offer 3 names or take theirs (never Claude, Anthropic or the brain's own tool names; folder = ASCII lowercase-dash, e.g. Zoë -> zoe, or a folder the human picks for a name with no Latin letters; the name is kept as display_name) -> Claude synthesises the details -> one-screen draft card -> revise until approved -> write the seven files from TEMPLATES -> `python3 ~/.claude/skills/persona-forge/validate_persona.py <folder>` (all PASS) -> `voidloom persona declare --name NAME --skill FOLDER --blurb ...` (merges persona.json with a backup) -> `bash ~/.claude/memory/install/wire_persona.sh FOLDER` after showing what it changes and asking -> store 3-5 dual-layer identity memories -> start a new session to meet it. Re-run /persona-forge to revise (foundation changes by proposal). `voidloom persona decline` writes a marker in the brain home and silences the reminder; `--undo` removes it. `voidloom doctor` reports the persona row as 'pending (not a failure)' until forged.
